title: Degenerated differential pair
description: A source-degenerated differential pair: a resistor $R_s$ in each source lifts the linear input range and improves offset at the cost of transconductance. The effective transconductance is $G_m = g_m/(1 + (g_m + g_{mb})*R_s)$; the degeneration factor $n_{deg} = 1 + (g_m + g_{mb})*R_s$ divides GBW and the input offset while the ~1-decade linear range extends to about $V^* + (I_{tail}/2)*R_s$. Entered from the COMMON MODE: the device's source node $V_s$ — its FULL elevation above the bulk, tail lift and resistor drop together — is the one free bias variable, pinned so the produced $CM_{in} = V_s + V_{GS}$ equals $CM_{dc}$. Both bias coordinates then follow outright ($v_{sb} = V_s$, $v_{ds} = V_{out} - V_s$), and the body effect is charged in full rather than only the resistor's few tens of millivolts. Degeneration's boost of the device output resistance is neglected here, so the gain into a fixed load conductance is a conservative estimate.

params.name: Av_target
params.note: gain target AFTER degeneration: n_deg divides the raw gm, so this is what is left once the linear range is bought

params.name: GBW_target
params.note: bandwidth target after degeneration, same trade as the gain target

params.name: linrange_target
params.note: required single-ended linear input range (differential is roughly twice this)

params.name: vn_target
params.note: input-referred thermal density budget, set above the 32.5 nV/rtHz floor measured on a sky130 tt realization of this pair rather than above the gamma-model estimate — a budget that only clears the model is not a budget. The degeneration resistor's own 4kT*R_s is the linearity price: at the default 12 kOhm it is most of the modelled power, and the row lands near 25 nV/rtHz

params.name: CM_lo
params.note: input CM range the application presents, low edge — proven exactly by the cm-lo edge at every evaluation (the sweep put the widest closing range at 0.85-1.32 V on sky130 tt at the shipped choices). The edge proves the ENDPOINT; the interior is the sweep's to show

params.name: CM_hi
params.note: input CM range the application presents, high edge — its ENDPOINT proven by the cm-hi edge the same way

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: the input common mode the application presents. The engine places the source node so the sheet sits exactly here; sweep it to trace the common-mode axis

params.name: V_out_dc
params.note: drain DC level; sets the input device vds

params.name: V_s
params.note: the input device's source node — its full elevation above the bulk, tail lift plus the resistor drop. Solved rather than set: bisected between min and max (the BRACKET) until the produced common mode equals CM_dc

params.name: R_s
params.note: per-side degeneration resistance; (gm + gmb)*R_s sets the linearization and offset improvement

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion; high gm/ID makes degeneration more effective (larger (gm + gmb)*R_s)

doc.title: Input-pair device (degenerated)
doc.description: Half-circuit input device at half the tail current, with R_s in its source. Its source node V_s is the sheet's one free bias variable: vsb = V_s (the FULL elevation above the bulk, not just the resistor lift) and vds = V_out_dc - V_s.

params.name: vsb_i
params.note: the source node — the device's full elevation above the bulk

rows.name: CM_in
rows.note: the input common mode this bias produces — an OUTPUT here, not a setting; rises monotonically with the source node, so the pin is a well-posed bisection

rows.name: n_deg
rows.note: degeneration factor; Gm, GBW, and vos all scale by 1/n_deg. The source node carries the source-body generator's current through the same resistor, so gmb degenerates alongside gm — on a sky130 tt realization of this pair that takes the factor from 2.68 to 3.07 and lines Gm_eff and GBW up with the measured transfer instead of leaving them ~11% high. The device's own gds returns to the source node too, but at these impedances it is worth under 1% of the factor and is left out

rows.name: Rout
rows.note: the resistance this stage presents at its output: the input device's own output conductance in parallel with the estimated load conductance. Like the gain built on it, this neglects the degeneration boost the source resistor also gives the device r_o — so the row reads LOW, which is conservative for gain but not for loading: a parent checking a ratio against it will clear the check more easily than the real node would allow. The gain assumes a capacitive load, so nothing here models a resistive one; this row is what a composing parent checks its own loading against

rows.name: Av
rows.note: conservative: neglects the degeneration boost of the device output resistance

rows.name: vos_undeg
rows.note: the un-degenerated Pelgrom offset of the input pair

rows.name: vos
rows.note: degeneration divides the offset by n_deg (the gm-mismatch term is linearized away)

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: device density plus the degeneration resistor's 4kT*R_s, both sides of the pair (estimate)

rows.name: cgg_in
rows.note: estimate: the capacitance one input terminal presents — the gate capacitance of a single input device. Gate capacitance only, because the Miller term needs the gate-drain fraction and these tables do not carry it, so a driving stage sees more than this. No rule reads it

rules.note: degeneration must extend the linear range to the target
computed from the gamma-model floor; this table carries no measured noise; the simulator owns noise sign-off
trips when the source node is pushed so high the device runs out of drain-source voltage at the drain DC level
the common mode this bias produces has to sit inside the range the application presents
paired with cm-not-below; the cm-lo/cm-hi edges prove the range ENDS close, and the CM_dc sweep shows the whole landscape

edges.name: cm-lo
edges.note: the claimed low edge, proven exactly: the whole sheet re-evaluates at CM_dc = CM_lo — its own tail-node solve from the full bracket, its own devices — and every hard rule must hold there

edges.name: cm-hi
edges.note: the claimed high edge, proven the same way. Edges prove the ENDPOINTS; the CM_dc sweep remains the authority on the full landscape
